items.title: Albert "June" Gardner Interview, 1996-04-17
items.q: My father too, but my mother, she was always there for me, you know.

ctx.x: No regrets. So was your mother an influence on your life? Very much so, yeah. It seems that.

My father too, but my mother, she was always there for me, you know. It was always up front, you know, like don't lie to me. Tell me what it was. As a matter of fact, she died. I was always with Sam Cooke. I was home. And I had the doctor for her, because I was in and out of town. And I left and I went to Philadelphia. And we went to Uptown Theater. And I got a call that she had passed in 61. I stayed about four or five days. And I went back. I had to get back on the road. And I was in and out of town. And I was…
I stayed about four or five days.
